name: task-breakdown-rust
description: Turns a goal, spec or messy brief you type or paste into a structured work plan: 3-6 phases named by outcome, small tasks with ids, relative sizes (S/M/L/XL), dependencies, 1-3 acceptance criteria and owner placeholders. Code computes the order of work, the parallel waves, the critical path in relative units, per-phase totals and lanes for a team of N. Also emits a downloadable task_plan.md. Revise it in the same chat (split T4, merge T2 and T3, add a security review phase, we are 2 people, make it a 2-week plan for one engineer: code fits the plan to the timebox and lists what it deferred) and ask about it (critical path?, what depends on T5?) without re-planning. Stateless: it keeps nothing between messages, so follow-ups work on the plan still visible in the recent conversation; if a long plan has dropped out of it, paste the plan (or its task_plan.md) again. It never asks back: a request with no goal gets a one-line ask. It never invents owners, dates or tools and creates nothing in a tracker: the plan is a draft. Not for writing the deliverable itself or general questions. This is the Rust build: the same task breakdown as a small native binary.
